attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his own post. He cites Ramp data for the 1% figure, but the dependency claim is his inference.

semantics.note: Fair restatement of a dependency claim. In context 'their' refers to the startups, and the passage narrows to startups that subsidise token use. The contract notes that narrowing.

contract.note: The plain reading (startups can't keep paying the labs without new VC) is ordinary and fair. The result depends on which startups count as the cohort, which the speaker did not name, and on the evaluator choosing August 2026 as the period.

evidence.note: Harvey's own announcement of a $550M raise (Sep 9, 2026). It confirms Harvey raised money but not that it is in Ramp's top 1% or that its model bills depend on new VC.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not identify the startups in the top 1% and has none of their cash-flow or model-bill records. A funding announcement cannot show dependency, and nothing contradicts the claim either. The evidence does not settle the causal claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast sentence in his own post.

semantics.note: The normalised text drops 'dramatically' from 'get dramatically worse', which weakens the commitment. The contract's source elements put it back. 'Next year' = 2027 and the capacity mechanism are kept. Firm 'going to' makes this a scored forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'next year' as 2027 and treating capacity coming online as the mechanism, not a condition, is fair. 'Substantial' and 'dramatic' have no thresholds, so the reading decides the result.

evidence.note: Google Cloud release (Apr 2026) saying Anthropic TPU capacity is expected from 2027. It is a plan, not proof of payments or monthly escalation.

reviews.rationale: The forecast covers calendar 2027, which has not begun at the 2026-10-28 evaluation date. No irreversible event meeting the early-resolution rule appears in the packet. Not yet scorable.

attribution.note: Zitron's own observation about cases he examined.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'virtually every case I've found' scope, the subsidy description, and the full or slightly-discounted pricing detail.

contract.note: Limiting to his examined cases and defining a subsidy as allowed usage costing well above the subscription is a fair plain reading. The population is unnamed and August 2026 was chosen by the evaluator, so the claim is hard to check, not unfair.

evidence.note: Cursor's July 2025 pricing post: $20 of usage at API prices, with overage charged at cost. This cuts against heavy subsidy for Cursor, but it predates the period and shows no supplier invoices or discounts.

reviews.rationale: Zitron's examined cases are not identified, and the packet has no August 2026 allowances, invoices or discounts. The only item is an older Cursor pricing post, which is context. It neither supports nor contradicts the claim for the period.

attribution.note: Zitron's own forecast sentence, including his own parenthetical doubt.

semantics.note: Firm 'going to' about the 2027 start is a scored forecast. The parenthetical doubt is kept in his words and undercuts the 'every year following' part rather than adding a condition.

contract.note: Fair for the 2027 ramp. 'In earnest' and 'dramatically' have no thresholds, so the reading matters. Scoring later years against him would be questionable, since he doubted the bubble lasts that long. That does not apply before the horizon.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own Apr 2026 Amazon announcement on capacity timing and a $100B+ ten-year commitment. It is not an annual payment series and cannot show a 2027 ramp.

reviews.rationale: The dated part of the forecast is the 2027 ramp, and 2027 has not started by the evaluation date. No conclusive event is in the packet. The open-ended annual growth cannot yet be seen.
